answer: A beacon registry anchors each agent identity to a stake locked for a full epoch and slashed when one operator is caught running duplicate agents. New identities begin at dawn with zero reputation and must earn attestation from independent peers before transacting, so a Sybil farm cannot simply spawn thousands of cheap copies. Every verified action sends a ripple of cross-checks through the network: peers re-verify a sample of the agent history, and the cost of forging that history across many identities grows faster than the reward, making mass forgery unprofitable.
